Read the passage provided (Text A — a non-fiction article about restoring a wetland).

How does the writer help us understand the significance of caring for the natural environment? You might consider how they have used:
• mood and purpose
• descriptions of the landscape and wildlife
• ideas about responsibility and hope.

Support your answer with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Identify and describe aspects of the text that are relevant to the question; explain how one or more aspects create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together to build meaning across the text. Excellence: Explain how aspects have been deliberately chosen to create meanings and effects that connect to the writer's purpose and broader contexts. Look for: positive, hopeful tone that shifts from concern to optimism; vivid sensory descriptions of the wetland before and after restoration; use of statistics or facts balanced with personal reflection; metaphor or personification applied to the land or water; inclusive language (we, our) suggesting collective responsibility; contrast between degradation and renewal.

questions.text:
Read the poem provided (Text B — a poem about childhood summers).

How does the poet help us understand the speaker's feelings about growing up? You might consider how they have used:
• mood and purpose
• imagery and descriptions of place
• ideas about freedom and loss
• contrasting perspectives.

Support your answer with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Identify and describe aspects of the text that are relevant to the question; explain how one or more aspects create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together to build meaning across the text. Excellence: Explain how aspects have been deliberately chosen to create meanings and effects that connect to the writer's purpose and broader contexts. Look for: nostalgic or bittersweet tone achieved through word choice; sensory imagery (warmth, water, sunlight) evoking carefree childhood; contrast between the child's perspective and the adult's hindsight; use of past tense and present tense to show distance; enjambment or lack of punctuation suggesting freedom; a shift in mood towards the end signalling awareness of change.

questions.text:
Read the passage provided (Text C — a personal narrative about a grandparent's workshop).

How does the writer help us understand the importance of the relationship with their grandparent? You might consider how they have used:
• language to describe the grandparent and the workshop
• ideas about learning and patience
• ideas about objects and memory.

Support your answer with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Identify and describe aspects of the text that are relevant to the question; explain how one or more aspects create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together to build meaning across the text. Excellence: Explain how aspects have been deliberately chosen to create meanings and effects that connect to the writer's purpose and broader contexts. Look for: detailed sensory descriptions of the workshop (smells of wood, sounds of tools) that create atmosphere; the grandparent characterised through actions rather than direct description; simile or metaphor connecting the craft to wider ideas about care or skill; contrast between the child's impatience and the grandparent's steadiness; objects as symbols of connection, legacy, or love; a reflective or appreciative tone that deepens over the course of the text.
